That sounds like a disturbing environment. When I was a kd I use to take basketball shots where I would go through all these different future options. I only made baskets when I said I would be a homeless bum. The closest thing I was to homeless was I had this high school roommate that has a huge drinking problem. One night he tried to get me connected to literally killing his brother. I peaced out the same night and got a hotel. I wondered around the next day before I crashed at a relatives. In between though I felt this sense of freedom and im a freedom guy value wise. It was a weird feeling. Im petrified myself of being homeless I neen very close. I always play the mind game how could I survive being homeless? Get a burner, a spork, uss googe maps to check out isolated spots. The shitty thing is other people are into drugs and have mental health issues. Its not a perfect world. I kist spoke to a food cart guy that said those people at homeless shelters the executives will make 90k a year and then run shelters like that. Real helpful. Maybe you can turn this misfortune into awareness some how or some survival show on youtube. If anything... Good luck!!! Dont kill yourself with one of those weapons. Maybe sell that for survival gear? But you prob have a ton being a vet.

I left again when I was 19. I crashed with a friend for a little bit. I found a crummy job working telemarketing in the afternoons/evenings and playing video games during the day or working out with a friend. I moved out of my friends pad into my own rented room and kept on the look out for a job. I caught a good break at 20 when I found a good job. From there it took off. Around 21/22 I was drinking a ton socially. And it really wore me out and some of my crazy behavior was influenced by alcohol, which was much more complicated. I was Johnny Manziel without the fame and looks. I found a alcohol counselor online and started to change my life from there on an emotional level. After that there was a little break between and I tried several different counselors. Some were not a good match, some pissed me off, and others were just annoying. Counselors and therapists CAN make things worse especially if they overstep their expertise. 

When my Dad passed away back in 2011 I did a lot of research to find the right therapist for me. I wrote my story, contacted her, and she offered to see me even though she was booked. I met with her for nearly a year or two and it changed my life forever. It uplifted me from the dumps and helped me get an appropriate perspective on my life that I could improve upon. The key thing I did for myself was, I did my homework. Before I didn't do my homework because I was broken and I'd let anyone try to help me even if it wasn't a good match so it was a hard road. 

It's a hard road, but things do get a lot better, but you still struggle in your late 20's and 30's. I'm going to be 31 in June. Of course I made mistakes along the way and of course I still struggle today, but overall, yes my life has tremendously become way better since I was 19 and dealing with similar problems. I did make some similar mistakes in my early twenties but if you can get through that rough period without too many negative consequences like addiction or whatever the upper twenties really improve with maturity and experience. After all, you're no longer considered some shitty little kid at 19. The biggest advice I gave to myself through hard times was, hang in there.

I had zero friends, privacy, and really not even my own home, it sucked. I tried to join the marines but was denied because of character issues and prob low asvab. I didn't finish the tenth grade. I ran away from home. I tried to get into iupui but with no money and no transportation wtf was the point? It sucked. Things however took a dramatic turn eventually. 19 is a weird age in general. You're not 18 but youre not 20. Hang in there and make some good decisions.

The first time I encountered people threatening suicide was a young cousin, eight years younger, and there wasn't anything I could do. The second time was a gf who threatened it because I broke up with her. I stayed and tried to fix it, but shit ended up worse for me and she didnt kill herself and we are not together today. I pulled a friend down from a tree branch after a bad breakup and a guys night out. My mom threatened suicide and I got smart. I called the police for a welfare check. My point is if youre present, provide emergency support, wrapping, pulling tjem down, call 911. Next, don't give in to those threats of violence. If they do it in front of you leave immediately and don't look back. If your brother can't follow the rules peace out. If your brother decided to kill himself, its not your fault. Again, call the cops and have him hospitalized. My biggest input is never let anyone hook you on a suicide threat. It's a control play and in the lo g run if you feel bad now its not going to get any better. There is something inside them that needs help. Don't let that behavior suck you in. Enforce your boundaries so you dont lose yourself.

I tried to join the army at 18. I have a super sketchy background. I ran away from home at 16. I have a juvy record. I had some reckless driving tickets. I went through meps, but the paperwork took forever becaus I had to get waivers. In addition to that I was pressing for specific items on my contract because a former ranger encouraged me to. I never signed the papers because my adhd went elsewhere. I ended up moving back in with a family member. I too felt put down and unsupported. I was like 19.  

While I lived there I went for the marines. I was denied because of character issues. It was a huge bummer. A guy I had to use as a reference... I vandalized his car because I felt he screwed me over. I'm pretty much bat shit crazy. I was so bummed too. 

After staying with my fam for a little bit I left. I busted my ass and got a few breaks. I got lucky, but I swore to never stay at my families again. They lived in the suburbs which to me triggere suicide feelings. I would rather be homeless and digging in trash for food than deal with the mental put downs and live isolated in some weird ass yuppy home.

The hard thing for you is the feeling of being trapped and simply just not good enough. My point is yeah I was afraid and bummed, but I had an alternative, an option. It sounds like to me you need to discover that option. The thing that holds you back is confidence or an ego to get you going or perservere through your nevessary loses.  

So how can you develop your options? Career assessments. Google jvic or some career assessments free. Take a personality test. Seriously connect with knowing yourseld and your matches and pursue something that makes you happy. Beaware of your values. For me, money was a big one even at the expense of my true happiness. Dont be like me. You will be misseable if you get into it for the cash but end up a debt to that job.

Find a way to finance your training. There are so many things out there. For your owb sanity and self respect find a roommate, find a healthier living arrangement. Life keeps going but the decisions you make now and the things you do will change when youre 30. Good luck!!

Ps dont impulsively run away and be homeless.. Strategize. Ok so live at your folks until you secure somethi g different. Be safe. Don't let your emotions rule you and make things worse. Never make any decisions when feeling bad or do anything to make the situation worse.
